candidates.title: Pacific Fusion — Experimental breakthrough clears major obstacle to affordable commercial fusion
candidates.notes: Already extracted in iter-03 as pacificfusion-updates-experimental-breakthrough-by-pacific.md. Contains: 22 MA, 4 shots over 5 days, 120 ns implosion time, Al layer thicknesses (50 µm vs 200 µm), B-dot probe field measurements. Confirms self-magnetizing target eliminates external copper coils. Future work: eliminate laser preheat. No gain values or fusion yield data.

candidates.title: ANS Nuclear Newswire — Fusion simplification demonstrated by Pacific Fusion and Sandia (Feb 2026)
candidates.notes: Not previously extracted. Describes the same Feb 2026 self-magnetizing target breakthrough. No quantitative performance data (no gain, no yield), but confirms experimental demonstration and context. Secondary source corroborating the breakthrough.

candidates.title: Simulated thermonuclear performance of auto-magnetizing helical liner MagLIF target implosions (Physics of Plasmas, April 2025)
candidates.notes: Peer-reviewed paper by Shipley et al. (2025) directly addressing G-11: 3D rad-MHD simulations of AutoMag helical liner implosions, >30 T axial B-field, higher thermonuclear yield vs standard MagLIF. AIP paywall — extraction failed.

candidates.title: Integrated simulations of premagnetized and self-magnetizing dynamic screw pinch-driven MagLIF (Physics of Plasmas, 2025)
candidates.notes: Another 2025 peer-reviewed paper on self-magnetizing MagLIF targets. Not attempted for extraction — AIP paywall likely.

candidates.title: Auto-magnetizing (AutoMag) liners for MagLIF: Helically-wound composite liners (OSTI technical report, 2016)
candidates.notes: 2016 Sandia technical report by Awe et al. — foundational AutoMag concept. PDF accessible via OSTI. Not extracted: 2016 origin limits relevance for current gain projections; 2025 Physics of Plasmas paper is the current state-of-art.
